intendedUse.primaryUse: Automated first-pass screening of job applications to identify candidates for human recruiter review
outOfScopeUses: Autonomous hiring decisions without human review
Evaluating candidates outside the trained domain

riskClassification.euAiActBasis: Annex III, Section 4(a): AI systems intended to be used for recruitment or selection, particularly for screening or filtering applications
riskClassification.riskJustification: 9 critical finding(s) detected. The system shows statistically significant bias that may constitute illegal discrimination.
riskClassification.humanOversightDescription: All screening decisions must be reviewed by a qualified human recruiter before any candidate is rejected. The system provides recommendations only.

trainingData.description: Foundation model (GPT-4 class) fine-tuned on 10,000 anonymized resume-outcome pairs from 2020-2024 hiring data
trainingData.demographicRepresentation: Unknown — the foundation model's training data composition is not publicly available
trainingData.dataGovernance: Foundation model training data is managed by the model provider. Fine-tuning data (if any) follows internal data governance policy.
trainingData.biasesInTrainingData: LLMs are known to encode societal biases from internet text corpora, including gender and racial stereotypes in professional contexts.

metrics.evaluationMethodology: Counterfactual testing with matched resume pairs differing only on demographic attributes (name, pronouns, graduation year). Statistical significance assessed via Welch's t-test and chi-squared test.

findings.detail: Decision flip rate of 36% is statistically significant (chi-squared=6.6316, p=0.010019).
findings.recommendation: Investigate the model's decision boundary for demographic sensitivity. Consider retraining with balanced data or adding post-processing fairness constraints.

findings.detail: Mean score difference of 0.79 points favoring "male" (t=4.8071, p=0.000017, Cohen's d=1.3596).
findings.recommendation: The model systematically scores one group higher. Audit training data for representation bias and consider score calibration.

findings.detail: Disparate impact ratio of 0.64 fails the 80% rule. This may violate EU AI Act requirements and US EEOC guidelines.
findings.recommendation: This level of disparity likely constitutes illegal discrimination. Do NOT deploy without mitigation. Consider threshold adjustment, model retraining, or human-in-the-loop review for the disadvantaged group.

mitigationSteps: IMMEDIATE: Halt automated screening for affected demographic groups until bias is remediated
Implement human-in-the-loop review for all candidate evaluations
Audit training data for demographic representation imbalances
Consider post-processing fairness constraints (equalized odds, demographic parity)
Implement continuous monitoring dashboards disaggregated by demographic group
Create incident reporting and appeals process for candidates
Train recruiters on system limitations and bias risks
residualRisks: Bias in attributes not tested (disability, religion, sexual orientation)
Subtle proxy discrimination through features correlated with protected attributes
Temporal drift — model behavior may change with updates
Intersectional bias in rare combinations may be undetected due to small sample sizes

potentialHarms: Qualified candidates from underrepresented groups may be systematically ranked lower
Proxy discrimination through university names or other correlated features
mitigationSteps: IMMEDIATE: Halt automated screening for affected demographic groups until bias is remediated
Implement human-in-the-loop review for all candidate evaluations
Audit training data for demographic representation imbalances
Consider post-processing fairness constraints (equalized odds, demographic parity)
Implement continuous monitoring dashboards disaggregated by demographic group
Create incident reporting and appeals process for candidates
Train recruiters on system limitations and bias risks

knownLimitations: Bias audit covers gender, ethnicity, and age but not all protected characteristics (disability, religion, sexual orientation)
Name-based testing captures explicit bias but may miss subtle proxy discrimination
Statistical tests require sufficient sample sizes — rare intersections may be undertested
The audit tests the system at a point in time — model behavior may change with updates
Counterfactual testing assumes name is the only signal — real resumes have correlated features
dataGaps: Limited coverage of non-binary gender identities
No testing for socioeconomic proxies (zip code, school type) beyond university name
performanceBoundaries: System is designed for professional/white-collar roles; may not generalize to trade/manual labor positions

conditions: DO NOT deploy for automated decision-making until critical findings are resolved
Engage external auditor for independent bias assessment
Conduct impact assessment per EU AI Act Article 9
Maintain audit logs for all screening decisions per EU AI Act Article 12
Provide candidates with explanation of screening criteria per EU AI Act Article 13
monitoringRequirements: Continuous monitoring of decision rates disaggregated by demographic group
Quarterly bias re-audit with updated test sets
Incident reporting mechanism for candidates who believe they were unfairly treated
Annual review by independent ethics board
humanOversight: All rejection decisions must be reviewed by a human recruiter
The system score must not be the sole factor in any hiring decision
Recruiters must be trained on the system's known biases and limitations
An appeal process must be available to all candidates
